title: Aug 23 · Adjectives that agree: -a / -i / -e
topic: Adjective agreement — the mera/meri/mere endings, now on adjectives — plus fruit & sabzi vocab

pattern.name: Adjectives agree with their noun
pattern.template: [ adjective + -a / -i / -e ]  +  [ noun ]   —   the noun decides the ending
notes: Same ending system as mera / meri / mere from Aug 16: -a masculine, -i feminine, -e plural or respect.
The adjective sits in front of its noun: bada bhai, khatti pani puri — or before hai: ghar bahut badaa hai.
bahut goes right before the adjective it boosts: bahut achha dancer.
Respect makes it plural, even for one person: mere bhaiya bahut patle hai.
Two words for old: bordha for living beings, purana for things.

vocab.note: badi (f) · bade (pl/respect); bada bhai = older brother — your sentence pages write bada
chhoti (f) · chhote (pl); chhota bhai = younger brother; page also: chota
achchhi (f) · achchhe (pl); your sentence pages mostly write achha / achhi
bordhi (f) · bordhe (pl/respect); for people and animals — things are purana; often spelled boodha
purani (f) · purane (pl); Taj Mahal bahut purana hai

sentences.en: My older brother is a very good dancer.
sentences.rom: Mera bada bhai bahut achha dancer hai.
sentences.note: the dancer is a he → achha; bada bhai = older brother

sentences.en: Your younger sister is not a good dancer.
sentences.rom: Tumhari chhoti behen achhi dancer nahi hai.
sentences.note: everything goes -i to match behen; nahi sits just before hai
unke from Aug 16; your page reads hai — plural 'are' is usually hai(n), on the Ask list

sentences.en: My new house is very big and beautiful.
sentences.rom: Mera nayaa ghar bahut badaa aur sundar hai.

sentences.note: your page looks like bordhe, but the day's system predicts bordhi for feminine grandma — ending unconfirmed, ask your teacher (meri vs mera is also hard to read on the page)

sentences.en: I don't want sour Pani Puri.
sentences.rom: Mujhe khatti Pani Puri nahi chahiye.
sentences.note: khatta → khatti to match pani puri (feminine); mujhe = mujhko from Aug 4; nahi before chahiye
purana, not bordha — the Taj is a thing

sentences.en: My younger brother is very fat, and my older brother is very skinny.
sentences.rom: Mera chhota bhai bahut mota hai, mere bhaiya bahut patle hai.
sentences.note: respect makes it plural: mere bhaiya … patle — the -e endings from Aug 16 finally in action
aapka = formal your; khana is masculine → kadwa

watch_out: The -e column is respect too: mere bhaiya bahut patle hai — one person, plural everything.
Two olds: bordha for living beings, purana for things. The Taj Mahal is purana; grandma is not.
The adjective agrees with the thing even in a chahiye sentence: Mujhe khatti Pani Puri nahi chahiye — khatti, because pani puri is feminine.
nahi still sits just before the verb part: achhi dancer nahi hai.
ask_next_time: Grandma: the page looks like bordhe, but grandma is feminine — bordhi hai(n) or bordhe hai(n)? Which ending do respected women get?
Sentence 3 reads nahi hai — should plural parents be nahi hai(n)?
Genders of the new fruits & sabzi — especially adrak and pyaaz — needed to pick khatta vs khatti at the market.
